programs.title: N-body
programs.what: naive = small functions and plain loops; optimized = hand-unrolled scalar statics (f64)

programs.title: Fannkuch-redux
programs.what: naive = helper functions; optimized = everything hand-inlined into main

programs.title: Spectral-norm
programs.what: naive = A(i,j) through a function; optimized = incremental denominator, no calls

programs.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
programs.what: naive = stdlib DynamicArray<u8> (get/set under bounds proofs); optimized safe = safe dynarray with bounds proofs; optimized unsafe = unsafe dynarray, no checks. C, C++ and Rust: free = release memory at the end, leak = do not

programs.title: String manipulation
programs.what: naive = stdlib String (appendChar/charAt/setCharAt per character); optimized = raw byte buffers, safe (bounds proofs) or unsafe. C, C++ and Rust: free or leak

programs.title: Heap graph search
programs.what: N nodes on the heap with four edges each, find a needle by breadth-first search. The other languages allocate every node separately and link them with pointers; Caspien structs may only point at themselves through a plain nullable `ref`, so there are two families: INDEX edges (naive/optimized rows: parallel arrays, or one dynarray of Node structs in the struct-node rows) and REF rows, where every node is its own heap object with four `ref` edges to other nodes, each node access under a ghost-table alive proof

programs.title: Sorting and searching
programs.what: quicksort, merge sort and heap sort of N random values, N binary searches and 20 linear searches. Caspien elements are u64 (the others use 32-bit ints)

programs.title: Binary trees
programs.what: allocate, walk and free many complete binary trees (a stretch tree, one long-lived tree, then 2^(N-d+4) trees of each depth d = 4, 6, .., N). The other languages use pointer nodes; Caspien has two families: an index-based tree (children are indices, 0 = null) in a dynarray of Node structs with a free list and an explicit work stack (naive uses one stdlib DynamicArray<Node>: get plus the pointer-taking setPtr), and the REF rows, where every node is a real heap object whose l/r are plain `ref` members of the same struct (alive proof per deref, owned by a pool of owns slots)

programs.title: Mandelbrot
programs.what: escape-time count over an N x N grid, at most 100 iterations per point; f64 scalar maths, no arrays or allocation (a single Caspien variant)

programs.title: FASTA generation
programs.what: LCG-driven repeat and weighted random sequences written into one heap buffer; prints length, checksum and letter counts (integer thresholds, no floating point)

programs.title: k-nucleotide (hash map)
programs.what: count k-mer frequencies for k = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 in a generated DNA sequence. C and the optimized Caspien variants use a hand-written open-addressing table; the other languages use their idiomatic maps; Caspien naive uses the stdlib HashMap. The LCG period is 139,968, so the tables stay small and cache-friendly

programs.title: LRU cache
programs.what: capacity 262,144 over 1,048,576 keys, 75% of operations on a hot subset, hash map plus recency list. Optimized Caspien: index-based doubly linked list and chained hash map in dynarrays; naive: stdlib DynamicArray + HashMap (no remove, evicted keys map to a sentinel)

programs.title: Merkle tree
programs.what: build a Merkle tree over N leaves, then generate and verify N/2 proofs (every 4th tampered). The hash is real SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4, hand-written in every language, no crypto library): one compression per leaf, two per internal node

programs.title: Hello World
programs.what: print one line: measures start-up time, compile time and binary size

programs.title: JSON serialise + parse
programs.what: hand-written serialiser writes N records to one text buffer, a hand-written iterative parser reads them back; every language does the same work (no JSON library). Naive keeps the records in one stdlib DynamicArray<Rec>

programs.title: Thread spawn
programs.what: N tasks (a multiple of 64) run in waves of 64 OS threads, each thread runs the same integer kernel on its own state and the results are added up after the join. No data is shared between threads. Only languages with OS-level threads are included.

programs.title: Swap lock contention
programs.what: 32 OS threads each update one shared (count, sum) struct N times under one lock (Caspien: a swap lock; the others: their standard mutex). The result does not depend on the order of the updates.
